v.q: You load 100 `Customer` rows and then access each customer's lazy `accounts` collection in a loop. What is this problem called?
v.w: One query for customers plus one query per customer. Fix with `JOIN FETCH`, an `@EntityGraph`, batch fetching or a DTO projection.

v.q: Which fix helps an N+1 problem?
v.w: Load the association in the same query instead of one query per row.

o: Loads the association only when it is first accessed
Loads every association at application startup
v.w: Accessing a lazy association after the session closes causes `LazyInitializationException`. Load what you need inside the transaction.

v.q: Which statement about lazy loading is NOT true?
o: It loads every association at startup
v.w: Eager loading does that. Lazy loading waits until the association is used.

v.q: Why is `spring.jpa.open-in-view=true` often switched off in production?
o: It holds a connection for the whole request and hides lazy loading in views
It switches lazy loading off completely for every entity
It only makes the application slower to start up
It forces every query in the request to be read-only
v.w: Fetch what the response needs inside the service layer, then map to DTOs.

v.q: Which property helps avoid holding a connection for the whole web request?
v.w: Open session in view keeps the persistence context open for rendering, which can hide lazy loading.

v.q: A repository declares `List<Customer> findByLastNameAndStatus(String lastName, String status)`. How does it work?
o: Spring Data derives the query from the method name
The SQL must be written in an XML file
Every row is loaded and filtered in memory
v.w: For complex queries use `@Query` (JPQL or native) or the Criteria API/Specifications.

v.q: Which method name is a valid derived query?
v.w: Spring Data parses property names and keywords such as OrderBy.

v.q: What does an entity in the managed state mean for `EntityManager`?
o: Changes are detected and flushed to the database at commit
The entity can no longer be modified
The entity lives only in a separate cache
The entity has already been deleted
v.w: This is dirty checking. You do not need to call `save()` again for an entity loaded in the same transaction.

v.q: Which entity state is tracked and flushed by the EntityManager?
v.w: Changes to a managed entity are saved at flush or commit without calling save again.

v.q: How does `@Version` help with concurrent updates?
o: Optimistic locking: the update fails if the version changed meanwhile
It locks the row until the transaction commits
It numbers the published versions of the REST API
It keeps a backup copy of the old row in another table
v.w: Hibernate adds `WHERE version = ?` to the update and throws `OptimisticLockException` when no row matches. Retry or tell the user.

v.q: Which statement about @Version is NOT true?
o: It locks the row until commit
v.w: It is optimistic locking, so nothing is locked while users work.

v.q: Why prefer a DTO projection over returning entities from a REST endpoint?
o: It selects only needed columns and avoids exposing internals
Entities can never be serialised to JSON by any library
DTOs are quicker for developers to type than entities
Entities never contain any data when they are loaded
v.w: Entities have lazy proxies and bidirectional links that cause recursion or leaks. DTOs give a stable API shape.

v.q: Which return type avoids exposing entity internals in a REST API?
v.w: A DTO shapes the response and avoids lazy loading surprises.

v.q: What does `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` on a query method help with?
o: Hibernate can skip dirty checking, and reads may go to a replica
It forbids every read operation inside the method
It blocks all other transactions until it finishes
It turns on the second-level cache for the whole entity
v.w: It is a hint, not a guarantee. It is commonly used on service methods that only read.

v.q: Which action is NOT helped by readOnly = true?
o: Saving memory in the persistence context
v.w: A read-only transaction is for queries. Writes are not intended there.
